assumptions: The fixture project is Harbor (harbor.so), an invoice app for freelancers. Project state holds reports/GROWTH_ONBOARDING_PLAN.md naming Harbor and what it does, one organic.audit evidence.json whose panel names Harbor with site_hosts harbor.so and app.harbor.so, and an earlier reports/brand-findability/ report with a score of 21, unless a case says otherwise.

Brand name, domain and category come from the inputs first and from project context when the inputs are empty. A run that can resolve neither brand nor domain writes a diagnostic and searches nothing.

The query plan, every status, the score, the verdict and the fixes come only from the SCORE.md functions. The model labels each result with one kind; the functions reject an own-host result labelled otherwise and a lookalike host labelled own.
Search results change over time, so live result pages are observations with a date, not fixtures. Run success establishes artifact delivery only.
cost_drivers: One bounded Codex session under the existing procedure ceiling, with no managed-model routes and no connected-provider calls.
Web actions: one search per planned query (max_queries, 4 to 16) and at most five page fetches, one of them the homepage. No measured live cost yet.
effects: Writes one run-owned reports/brand-findability/<run_id>.md in project state.
Reads the onboarding plan, organic audit evidence, project memory, the keyword plan and earlier brand-findability reports, plus public search results and pages through fenced web search.
No site change, pull request, post, form submission, contact, memory edit or workflow start. Fixes are text for the founder to act on or hand to the named workflow.

rubric.question: Is every query something a person who only heard the name would type, with no site filters, quotes or queries outside the planned set?
Is every result on the brand's own hosts labelled own, and is every same-named company, product, place or word labelled namesake rather than own, profile or about_brand?
Does every fix cite the actual results that show the problem, and is each action specific to this brand rather than general search advice?
When searches failed, does the report say which ones and withhold a verdict instead of guessing a score?

cases.description: Second run with empty inputs. The bare name, a common respelling and a mishearing are held by namesakes; the name with its category and the typed domain reach the site; the homepage title lacks the category. Expect the brand resolved from project context, a LOST verdict from the functions, the say-the-query fix first, and the score compared with last run.

Plausible but unusable provider responses: the search for the bare name times out and two more come back empty. An empty read is a failed read, not proof the brand is missing. The useful result is an incomplete report with no verdict, no score and no fixes, naming the failed searches.
A brand with a distinctive name whose site holds the first result for every query. The useful result is a FINDABLE verdict and no invented fixes.

A new project with empty brand_name and domain, and no onboarding plan, organic audit, keyword plan or project memory. The run must name what is missing and what to run, not guess a brand from the repository name.
